title: Modal Verbs — muset, moct, smět
description: Learn to conjugate the three Czech modal verbs — muset (must), moct (can/be able to), and smět (may/be allowed to) — and use them with infinitives in present-tense sentences.

data.heading: Modal Verbs
data.body: Must, can, may, want — snap them in front of any action and your sentences level up.
data.intro: Must, can, may, want — four verbs that instantly make you sound more grown-up in Czech. Snap them in front of any action and watch your sentences level up.

exercises.prompt: What is the 'já' (1st person singular) form of 'muset' (must)?

data.question_en: What is the 'já' (1st person singular) form of 'muset' (must)?
data.explanation: 'Muset' is an -et class verb. The 1st person singular is 'musím'. Conjugation: musím, musíš, musí, musíme, musíte, musí.

exercises.prompt: What is the 'ty' (2nd person singular) form of 'moct' (can)?

data.question_en: What is the 'ty' (2nd person singular) form of 'moct' (can)?
data.explanation: 'Moct' is irregular. The 2nd person singular is 'můžeš'. Full conjugation: mohu/můžu, můžeš, může, můžeme, můžete, mohou/můžou.

exercises.prompt: What is the 'oni' (3rd person plural) form of 'smět' (may/be allowed)?

data.question_en: What is the 'oni' (3rd person plural) form of 'smět' (may/be allowed)?
data.explanation: 'Smět' is an -et class verb. The 3rd person plural is 'smějí'. Conjugation: smím, smíš, smí, smíme, smíte, smějí.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the correct form of 'muset' for 'my' (we).

data.explanation: 'My musíme jít do školy.' = We must go to school. The 1st person plural of 'muset' is 'musíme'. The modal verb is followed by the infinitive 'jít'.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the correct form of 'moct' for 'on' (he).

data.explanation: 'On může mluvit česky.' = He can speak Czech. The 3rd person singular of 'moct' is 'může'. Modal verbs take the infinitive 'mluvit' after them.

exercises.prompt: Translate to Czech: 'I must work tomorrow.'

data.grammar_note: 'Musím' = I must (1st person singular of 'muset'). The infinitive 'pracovat' follows the modal. Word order is flexible: 'Musím zítra pracovat' or 'Zítra musím pracovat' are both correct.

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: 'Ona smí jít ven.'

accepted_answers: She is allowed to go out.
data.grammar_note: 'Smí' = may/is allowed to (3rd person singular of 'smět'). 'Jít ven' = to go out. 'Smět' specifically means permission, not ability.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the words to form: 'You can help us.'

data.explanation: 'Ty můžeš nám pomoci.' = You can help us. 'Můžeš' = you can (2nd person singular of 'moct'). 'Pomoci' = to help (infinitive). The modal verb 'můžeš' is followed by the infinitive 'pomoci'.

exercises.prompt: Match each modal verb to its English meaning.

data.prompt_en: Match each Czech modal verb to its English meaning.
data.explanation: 'Muset' = must (obligation), 'moct' = can (ability/possibility), 'smět' = may (permission). These are the three Czech modal verbs, each with a distinct meaning.

exercises.prompt: Match each conjugated form to the correct pronoun.

data.prompt_en: Match each conjugated form of 'moct' to the correct pronoun.
data.explanation: 'Moct' conjugation: já mohu/můžu, ty můžeš, on/ona může, my můžeme, vy můžete, oni mohou/můžou. Note the stem change from 'moh-' to 'můž-' in most forms.

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake in this sentence.

data.prompt_en: Find the mistake in this sentence using modal verbs.
data.explanation: The 2nd person singular of 'muset' is 'musíš', not 'musí'. 'Musí' is the 3rd person singular (on/ona musí) and 3rd person plural (oni musí). 'Ty musíš jít domů.' = You must go home.

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake in this sentence.

data.prompt_en: Find the mistake — wrong modal verb used.
data.explanation: 'Nesmíš' means 'you must not' (prohibition), while 'nemusíš' means 'you don't have to' (no obligation). The correct sentence is 'Nemusíš jít, pokud nechceš.' = You don't have to go if you don't want to. This is a common confusion between 'muset' and 'smět'.
